when: Consequential conditions, rules, contracts, histories, or proof boundaries must be modeled.
unless: The laws or invariants are already settled and only an implementable interface shape is needed.

when: Consequential conditions require an admitted domain, distinctions, assumptions, rules, forbidden cases, owners, or counterexamples.
Caller or callee obligations, preconditions, postconditions, failures, compatibility observers, replacement, or refinement are consequential.
Entities, intervals, cross-record integrity, quantified relations, identity, multiplicity, or set-versus-bag semantics determine valid instances.
Retry, stale or duplicate events, lifecycle, reorder, concurrency, safety, progress, stuttering, fairness, or temporal refinement is consequential.
A deductive implementation-conformance claim requires explicit specification, invariant, termination, proof-step, runtime-model, or trusted-boundary obligations.
Bounded search, satisfiability, feasibility, optimization, scope, encoding assumptions, witness meaning, or exact solver result states bound the claim.
Facts, rules, zero-one-many answers, proof multiplicity, duplicates, negation, binding order, search fairness, cycles, or divergence are consequential.
Initial state, goal, legal actions, intermediate invariants, action costs, equivalent plans, or no-plan meaning is consequential.
